targets.name: Explanatory mechanism — says WHY the approach should work
targets.instruction: Score 0-10 how far the abstract states a causal or conceptual reason the proposed approach should succeed — an insight, hypothesis, or mechanism linking a design choice to the effect it is expected to produce. Score low when the abstract only lists what was built and then asserts that it performs well.

targets.name: States the costs, limitations, or failure conditions of its own method
targets.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the abstract states any price paid for its gains — compute or memory overhead, a regime where the method degrades, a remaining unsolved part — rather than presenting an unqualified improvement.

targets.name: Ambition of the claim together with the specificity of the evidence offered for it
targets.instruction: Composite: first judge how large the abstract's central claim is (a field-level or community-level claim versus a narrow method claim), then judge how specific the evidence offered for that claim is; score 0-10 for the JOINT quality, giving high scores only when a big claim is matched by correspondingly concrete evidence and low scores when a big claim rests on vague evidence.

targets.name: Theoretical claims tied to the proposed method with stated scope
targets.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether any theory in the abstract is about the specific method or phenomenon at hand and its scope or assumptions are indicated (setting, model class, regime), rather than a generic mention that guarantees exist. Score NA when the abstract makes no theoretical claim at all.

targets.name: Reframing — recasts the problem in a different formalism or abstraction
targets.instruction: Score 0-10 how far the work re-describes a familiar problem inside a different formalism, abstraction, or level of description (rather than adding a component to the standard formulation). Score high when the abstract names both the old framing and the new one it substitutes.

targets.name: Motivation explains why the problem is hard, not merely that it is unaddressed
targets.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the opening motivation gives a substantive reason the problem resists existing approaches (a stated obstacle, tension, or structural difficulty), as opposed to noting only that it is understudied, underexplored, or that a gap exists.

targets.name: Breadth and diversity of the empirical evaluation actually enumerated
targets.instruction: Score 0-10 by how many genuinely distinct evaluation settings the abstract actually names — different tasks, benchmarks, modalities, languages, or model families — counting only settings that are stated, not promised. Score low when the evidence is one dataset or one task family.

targets.name: Technical specificity — the method's objects and operations are named precisely
targets.instruction: Score 0-10 on how precisely the abstract names the actual objects and operations of its method (what is parameterised, what is optimised, what is conditioned on what), such that a reader in the area could sketch the method's shape from the abstract alone. Score low for descriptions built out of generic nouns like framework, module, mechanism, strategy, and knowledge.

targets.name: Contributions are separable components each with a stated role
targets.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the abstract decomposes its contribution into distinct parts and says what each part is for, so a reader can tell which piece does which job. Score low when parts are listed but their individual purpose is not stated, and NA when there is only a single undivided contribution.

targets.name: Diagnoses a specific failure mode of prior work with stated evidence
targets.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the abstract identifies a concrete, named defect in existing approaches and gives some stated basis for the diagnosis (an analysis, an observation, a theoretical argument), as opposed to asserting that prior work is limited or insufficient.

targets.name: Reports a surprising, negative, or self-undercutting finding
targets.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the abstract reports at least one result that runs against the expected or convenient direction — a method that fails, a baseline that unexpectedly wins, a widely held assumption contradicted, or the authors' own approach falling short somewhere.

targets.name: Generality demonstrated beyond the primary setting rather than asserted
targets.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the abstract shows the contribution working outside the setting it was designed for — a second architecture, a second domain, a much larger scale — as reported evidence. Score low when generality is only claimed ('plug-and-play', 'can be applied to any ...') without a reported case.

targets.name: Quantified headline result against a named baseline or prior record
targets.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the abstract's central empirical claim is given as a specific number placed against a specifically named baseline, prior system, or record (e.g. 'X to Y on benchmark Z', '+N points over method M'). Score low for unquantified claims such as 'achieves state-of-the-art performance' or numbers with no stated comparison point.

targets.name: Human or expert judgment used as evaluation evidence
targets.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the evaluation includes judgments by people (human raters, domain experts, user studies, expert-annotated ground truth) rather than resting entirely on automatic metrics. Score by what the abstract states was actually collected.

targets.name: Discriminative evaluation — designed to decide between hypotheses, not to demonstrate the method
targets.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract poses a question with more than one possible answer, and separately whether the reported evaluation is structured to distinguish those answers (comparisons that could have come out the other way, ablations that isolate a cause); score 0-10 for the two TOGETHER. Score low when the evaluation exists only to show the proposal wins.

targets.name: Cost stated TOGETHER WITH gain, so the trade is checkable
targets.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract quantifies what its method gains, and separately whether it quantifies what the method costs (compute, latency, accuracy given up, extra passes); score 0-10 for BOTH being given in commensurable terms, so a reader could decide whether the trade is worth taking.

targets.name: Limiting result stated TOGETHER WITH the conditions under which it holds
targets.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract reports a limitation, failure, or negative finding, and separately whether it states the conditions that determine when the finding applies; score 0-10 for BOTH being present, low when a limitation is admitted without scope and low when scope is discussed but nothing limiting is reported.

targets.name: Theory and experiment coupled — the experiments test the theory's own prediction
targets.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract makes a theoretical claim, and separately whether the reported experiments are aimed at that claim (testing its assumptions, its predicted regime, or the instantiation it licenses) rather than at general performance; score 0-10 for the COUPLING. Score NA when neither theory nor experiment is present.

targets.name: Precise delta — prior work is characterised specifically enough that the change is checkable
targets.instruction: Composite: judge how specifically the abstract states what existing approaches actually do, and separately how specifically it states what its own contribution changes; score 0-10 for the two TOGETHER, so that a reader could verify the delta. Score low when prior work is described only as limited, insufficient, or underexplored.

targets.name: Derivation coupling — the problem's structure is established first and the method is derived from it
targets.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract establishes some structural fact about the problem (an observation, a formal property, a diagnosis) BEFORE naming its method, and separately whether the method is presented as following from that fact; score 0-10 for the two TOGETHER, low when a method is announced first and justified afterwards.

targets.name: Generality of the formal statement TOGETHER WITH concreteness of its instantiation
targets.instruction: Composite: judge how general the abstract's central formal or conceptual statement is, and separately how concretely it is instantiated (a specific algorithm, system, or construction that a reader could implement); score 0-10 for BOTH, low when a general statement stays abstract and low when a concrete system carries no general statement.

targets.name: Subsumption — prior work is exhibited as special cases of a more general statement
targets.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the work states a general formulation and shows that existing approaches fall out of it as special cases or instances, rather than sitting alongside them as one more alternative. Score high only when the abstract names what is being subsumed.

targets.name: Reusable artifact — what is left behind is fit for others to build on, judged scale-free
targets.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the work leaves an artifact others could genuinely build on — a dataset, benchmark, framework, or released system — judged by its novelty, documentation, and fitness for reuse. Judge scale-free: a small, well-specified, genuinely new artifact scores HIGH and a very large but routine or undocumented one scores LOW.

targets.name: Mechanistic explanation of an OBSERVED fact, not of the proposed method
targets.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the abstract explains WHY some empirically observed behaviour occurs — a property of existing systems, data, or the problem — as distinct from explaining why the authors' own method works. Score NA when no empirical observation about the world is made.

targets.name: Simplicity of the solution RELATIVE TO the difficulty of the problem it solves
targets.instruction: Composite: judge how hard the abstract establishes its problem to be, and separately how simple the proposed solution is (few moving parts, little machinery, minimal changes to existing systems); score 0-10 for the RATIO, high when a hard problem is met with a strikingly economical solution and low when an easy problem needs elaborate machinery.

targets.name: Names and characterises a phenomenon that did not previously have a name
targets.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the work isolates a recurring effect or failure mode, gives it a name, and characterises it well enough that others could look for it elsewhere — as opposed to naming its own method or system.

targets.name: Insight portability — the finding would survive replacing the specific benchmark it was shown on
targets.instruction: Composite: judge how tied the abstract's central finding is to the particular dataset, benchmark, or system used to establish it, and separately how the finding is phrased (as a fact about the world versus a fact about a leaderboard); score 0-10 for portability, high when the finding would still mean something if the benchmark were swapped.

targets.name: Assumption load TOGETHER WITH the strength of what is concluded from it
targets.instruction: Composite: judge how many and how restrictive the stated assumptions are, and separately how strong the conclusion drawn under them is; score 0-10 for the RATIO — high when a strong conclusion follows from mild or clearly stated assumptions, low when a strong conclusion rests on heavy or unstated ones.

targets.name: Internal consistency — the closing claim matches the opening claim in strength
targets.instruction: Composite: judge the strength of the contribution promised in the abstract's opening framing, and separately the strength of what is asserted in its closing sentences; score 0-10 for CONSISTENCY between them, low when the abstract escalates at the end beyond what the body of the abstract supports.

targets.name: Limitation-remedy correspondence — each named limitation has its own matched fix
targets.instruction: Composite: judge how specifically the abstract enumerates limitations of prior work, and separately whether each enumerated limitation is answered by a distinct, identifiable remedy; score 0-10 for the one-to-one CORRESPONDENCE, low when limitations are listed but the response is a single undifferentiated system, and low when remedies appear without stated limitations.

targets.name: Attribution — which component produces the gain, stated TOGETHER WITH the gain
targets.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract reports an improvement with a magnitude, and separately whether it attributes that improvement to an identified part of the method rather than to the system as a whole; score 0-10 for BOTH together. Score low for a headline number with no attribution and low for a story about mechanism with no magnitude.

targets.name: Establishes the problem is hard AND that it is nonetheless tractable
targets.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract gives a concrete reason the problem resists solution (a complexity result, a structural obstacle, a documented failure), and separately whether it shows the obstacle can actually be got around; score 0-10 for BOTH together.

targets.name: Efficiency gain stated TOGETHER WITH verified non-degradation
targets.instruction: Composite: judge how concretely the abstract quantifies a reduction in cost (compute, samples, memory, latency, annotation), and separately how explicitly it establishes that quality was NOT lost in exchange; score 0-10 for BOTH together, low when a saving is claimed without a parity check and low when parity is asserted with no quantified saving.

targets.name: Claim scope matches method scope
targets.instruction: Composite: judge how broad the abstract's stated contribution is, and separately how broad the method or analysis actually demonstrated is; score 0-10 for the MATCH between them — high when a narrow method is claimed narrowly or a broad method is genuinely shown broadly, low when the claim is wider than what was done.

targets.name: Prior failure demonstrated TOGETHER WITH a fix aimed at exactly that failure
targets.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract establishes that existing approaches fail in some concrete way — ideally shown rather than asserted — and separately whether the proposed method is targeted at that specific failure rather than being a general improvement; score 0-10 for the two TOGETHER.

targets.name: Negative space — what the method does not do, stated alongside what it does
targets.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract delimits its contribution — the regime it does not cover, the case it does not handle, the question it leaves open — and separately whether it is clear about what it does deliver; score 0-10 for BOTH together. Score low both for an unbounded claim and for a work described only by its boundaries.

targets.name: Overturns a stated prior belief — the old belief is named and the evidence against it is given
targets.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract explicitly names a belief, assumption, or expectation that the field currently holds, and separately whether it presents evidence or argument that this belief is wrong or incomplete; score 0-10 for BOTH together. Score low when a result is merely reported without contact with any prior expectation, and low when a prior belief is invoked but nothing is offered against it.

targets.name: Reinterpretation TOGETHER WITH the machinery it unlocks
targets.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract re-describes a familiar object as a different kind of object, and separately whether it names the specific new tools, architectures, or algorithms that this re-description makes available; score 0-10 for BOTH, low when a reinterpretation is offered with no consequence and low when new machinery appears without a reinterpretation motivating it.

targets.name: Currency of the comparison TOGETHER WITH the margin over it
targets.instruction: Composite: judge how current and strong the methods being compared against are (named, recent, credible competitors versus generic or dated baselines), and separately how clearly the margin over them is stated; score 0-10 for BOTH together.

targets.name: Structural property of an existing system identified TOGETHER WITH being exploited
targets.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract identifies a specific structural or behavioural property of an existing method, model, or data regime, and separately whether the proposed work turns that property into leverage; score 0-10 for the two TOGETHER. Score low when a property is merely observed and low when a fix arrives with no property behind it.

targets.name: Imported tool TOGETHER WITH justification that the analogy holds
targets.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the work brings in machinery from another field or subfield AND gives a reason the transfer is legitimate (a structural correspondence, a shared formal property), as opposed to applying an external technique because it is available. Score NA when nothing is imported.

targets.name: Provable guarantee TOGETHER WITH demonstrated practicality
targets.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract states a formal guarantee (a rate, bound, convergence, or optimality result), and separately whether it shows the method is practical to run (efficiency, simplicity, or empirical competitiveness); score 0-10 for BOTH together. Score NA when neither is claimed.

targets.name: Leaves a transferable design principle, not only a method
targets.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract states a lesson or principle a reader could apply outside this paper's specific method, and separately whether that principle is grounded in the reported results rather than merely suggested; score 0-10 for BOTH together.

targets.name: Corrects a specific prior claim rather than adding to a pile
targets.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the contribution is positioned as correcting, qualifying, or overturning an identifiable prior claim or widely-held position, as opposed to adding one more method to an existing family. Score low for 'we propose X, which outperforms Y'.

targets.name: Evaluation conditions match the conditions the claim is about
targets.instruction: Composite: judge what conditions the abstract's claim is about (a deployment setting, a scale, a data regime), and separately whether the reported evaluation was run under those conditions; score 0-10 for the MATCH. Score low when a claim about practice is supported only by small or idealised experiments.

targets.name: Necessity established — an ablation shows the components are actually required
targets.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract claims particular components are essential, and separately whether it reports an ablation or controlled comparison establishing that necessity; score 0-10 for BOTH together. Score low for components asserted as key with no ablation, and low for an ablation mentioned with no necessity claim attached.

targets.name: Checks whether a trivial approach would have sufficed
targets.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the abstract reports comparing against a deliberately trivial, naive, or degenerate alternative — random selection, the unmodified baseline, a no-op — in order to establish that the proposed machinery is needed at all. Score NA when no comparison of any kind is reported.

targets.name: Methodological critique — a flawed practice in the field is named AND its consequence shown
targets.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract identifies a specific defective practice in how the field evaluates, reports, or measures things, and separately whether it demonstrates what that defect costs (a wrong conclusion it produces, a method it falsely flatters); score 0-10 for BOTH together. Score low when a practice is criticised without demonstrated consequence.

targets.name: Simplicity restoration — a simple or classical method is shown to match or beat elaborate recent ones
targets.instruction: Composite: judge how simple the method being advocated is (few parts, classical, little tuning, small code change), and separately how elaborate the approaches it is shown to match or beat are; score 0-10 for the CONTRAST. Score low when a simple method beats only other simple methods, and low when the advocated method is itself elaborate.

targets.name: Cost accounting includes the method's own overhead
targets.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract reports a saving or speedup, and separately whether the accounting visibly includes what the method itself costs (its training, its extra passes, its added parameters); score 0-10 for BOTH together. Score low for a headline speedup whose own overhead is not accounted for.

targets.name: Reports the number a skeptic would ask for
targets.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the abstract volunteers the specific quantity most likely to undercut its own claim — the accuracy given up for a speedup, the failure rate, the gap remaining to a stronger method, the cost of the fix — rather than only the quantity that flatters it.

targets.name: Includes a condition under which the method is expected to do badly
targets.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the reported evaluation includes a setting chosen to stress or break the proposed approach — an adversarial case, an out-of-distribution regime, a condition the authors expect to be hard — as opposed to only favourable settings. Score NA when no evaluation is reported.

targets.name: Unification — one mechanism handles problems previously treated separately
targets.instruction: Composite: judge how many genuinely distinct problems the abstract claims to address, and separately how single the mechanism addressing them is; score 0-10 for BOTH together — high when one clean mechanism covers several previously separate problems, low for a multi-part system covering several problems and low for one mechanism covering one problem.

targets.name: The motivating observation is itself reported as a finding
targets.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract states an empirical observation that motivated the work, and separately whether that observation is presented as something the authors established rather than assumed or cited; score 0-10 for BOTH together.

targets.name: Credits what prior work got right while stating what it missed
targets.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract acknowledges a genuine contribution of the work it builds on or displaces, and separately whether it states specifically what that work leaves unsolved; score 0-10 for BOTH together. Score low for prior work described only as limited, and low for prior work praised with no gap identified.
